images.title: Four arms, four turns
images.purpose: Show that moving the red arm onto each of the four arms in turn gives the angles 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees.
images.composition: The windmill on the left, large and centred vertically, and a short list of four turns in a column on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: one windmill with 4 equal teal #0072B2 arms in a plus shape and a centre dot, the top arm coloured reddish purple #CC79A7, and a grey #6B7280 curved arrow from the red arm to the right arm. The arms are exactly 90 degrees apart. Right: a column of the 4 turn labels, one under another. Exactly 1 windmill, 1 red arm, 1 arrow, 4 list lines.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
arms of different lengths or gaps that are not equal
images.takeaway: Equal arms spaced equally give four angles of symmetry.
images.description: A four armed teal windmill with one red arm and a quarter turn arrow, beside the list 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to move the red arm one, two, three and four arms round and say each angle.

image_decisions.why: The list of turns of an equal armed windmill is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
